problem:
Title: Proof by Strong Induction: $n = 2^a b,\, b\,$ odd, every natural a product of an odd and a power of 2

Can someone guide me in the right direction on this question?

Prove that every $n$ in $\mathbb{N}$ can be written as a product of an odd integer and a non-negative integer power of $2$.

For instance: $36 = 2^2(9)$ , $80 = 2^4(5)$ , $17 = 2^0(17)$ , $64 = 2^6(1)$ , etc...

Any hints in the right direction are appreciated (please explain for a beginner).
Thanks.
proof_numbered:
0001 | Proof:
0002 | 
0003 | By the fundamental theorem of algebra, every integer $N$ can be uniquely factored as $\prod^{n}_{i=1}p_{i}^{a_{i}}$. Now, mark $2=p_{1}$, note $a_{i}$ can take value of $0$. You got the theorem. 
0004 | 
0005 | For the "inductive" proof, suppose for $n<k$ this is true. For $n+1$ its factors must be in previous $n$ numbers. Hence $n+1=\prod n_{i}$. Decompose $n_{i}$ by induction hypothesis you get the statement.
